Chat history now saves to a file after every turn. I tested the script on this session's transcript and it produced the files correctly. The hook itself hasn't fired yet: it can only run when a turn ends, and that hasn't happened since I set it up.

**What I set up**
- [.claude/settings.json](.claude/settings.json) adds a hook that runs when each turn ends, and again when the session closes.
- [.claude/hooks/save_chat_history.py](.claude/hooks/save_chat_history.py) reads Claude Code's full transcript and rebuilds these files from it every time:
  - `prompt_history/PROMPTS.md`: just your prompts, numbered in order.
  - `prompt_history/CHAT_HISTORY.md`: every session, oldest first, with each prompt, my reply and a folded list of the tools I used.
  - `prompt_history/sessions/*.jsonl`: an exact copy of each raw transcript, with nothing left out.
  - `prompt_history/sessions/*.md`: a readable version of each session.

Every run rewrites the files from the complete transcript, so one missed run loses nothing. Each run also refreshes sessions that were saved earlier, so turns a past session missed get filled in later.

**Two things you need to do**
1. **Start a new session.** The `.claude/` folder didn't exist when this session started, so Claude Code may not load the hook until a new session begins. Turns from this session will still be caught: the first run in the new session refreshes this one too. To save it right away instead, run:
   ```bash
   python3 .claude/hooks/save_chat_history.py ~/.claude/projects/-home-subhadip-Downloads-image-agents/fe7ebccf-b0ae-4e01-af8a-939468c84d35.jsonl
   ```
2. **Tell me about the older session.** There's a transcript from Nov 20 (`cab06061…`) for this project. I haven't included it. Do you want it in the history you submit?

I also saved a note to my memory never to delete `prompt_history/` or the hook during refactors.

I finished step 0 (the scaffold), but I haven't run the chat yet. The dev server won't start until wrangler is signed in to your Cloudflare account. Workers AI runs on Cloudflare's servers even in local dev, so it needs that login.

**What I did**
- Moved the Python project into `reference/`. The new TypeScript app is at the repo root.
- Pinned Node 22 in `.nvmrc`, because wrangler 4 doesn't support your default Node 20.
- Created a Worker with a React + Vite UI. `wrangler.jsonc` sets up Workers AI, an R2 bucket for images, Cloudflare Images (for resizing), and the chat agent.
- [src/server.ts](src/server.ts) defines `ImageChatAgent`, one per chat, which keeps message history in its own SQLite store. For now it just streams a Llama 3.3 reply; step 2 replaces that with the interpret → select → readiness → dispatch loop.
- [src/client/App.tsx](src/client/App.tsx) is a basic chat page. The chat id lives in the URL (`?chat=…`), so you can reload or share a chat.
- Wrote the build plan in [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md). It maps each of your four required components to its part of the app, covers the three agents, and lists steps 0–7.
- Typecheck and production build both pass.

**Choices I made while building**
- **Image model.** FLUX.2 klein accepts reference images only up to 512×512. The editor will shrink the current version with Cloudflare Images before sending it.
- **Voice.** The SDK has built-in voice input, but its docs mark it experimental and say it will break between releases. I plan to use a mic button that sends the recording to Whisper large v3 turbo instead.
- **Tests.** I removed `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`, which doesn't work with the current vitest. The orchestrator tests will run in plain Node with scripted model replies, like the Python tests did.

**What you need to do:** sign in once, in your own terminal:
```bash
cd ~/Downloads/image_agents && nvm use 22 && npx wrangler login
```
Then run `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:5173 to try the chat. Tell me when you're signed in and I'll check it from here.

Next is step 1: porting the schemas from `schemas.py`, defining the three agents (generator, editor, chitchat), and setting up the database tables for tasks and image versions. Should I go ahead? I can also run `git init` now so each step gets its own commit.

Chat now runs on OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini` using the key from your kognie-python project. I tested it in the browser: the reply streams in clean, one copy per token.

**Your key**
- I copied it from `~/kognie/Kognie-python/.env` into `.dev.vars`, which is git-ignored, so it won't be committed. I never printed it.
- When we deploy, it has to be uploaded to Cloudflare as a secret with `npx wrangler secret put OPENAI_API_KEY`. That sends the key to Cloudflare, so I'll ask you first.
- Your key also has access to `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.6-*` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`. To change the chat model, edit `CHAT_MODEL` in `wrangler.jsonc`.

**Why Llama looked bad:** most of it was a bug, not the model. Llama 3.3 sends every token in two fields, and the `workers-ai-provider` library (4.0.1) displayed both, which is why words appeared twice. I removed that library. If no OpenAI key is set, the app falls back to Llama 3.3 through my own small client in [src/llm.ts](src/llm.ts), which reads only one field.

**Other changes**
- `.dev.vars.example` documents the key. It also has an optional setting to send OpenAI calls through Cloudflare AI Gateway, which adds logging and caching and keeps a Cloudflare piece in the LLM path.
- [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) now lists OpenAI as the LLM.
- One gap: when the model call fails, the chat shows nothing at all instead of an error. That's how the first OpenAI attempt failed. I'll add an error message when I build the UI in step 5.

**Decision for you:** the image models. Should the generator and editor also use OpenAI? Your kognie project uses `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, which is much better at instruction edits and text in images than FLUX.2 klein. The trade-offs are cost and losing Cloudflare-native image generation. Other options are FLUX for generating and OpenAI for editing, or keeping FLUX for both.

Once you pick, I'll start step 1: the schemas, the three agents and the database tables.
